thread:
jess (support): customer on hosted API (acct: acme-inc) reporting sudden 502/504s starting ~09:10 UTC, ~30% of calls failing; they attached sample trace IDs and curl repro. high severity from their side. 

mike (sre): thanks. can you paste one trace id and a short repro? any recent deploys? :eyes:

jess (support): trace: trace-0a12b3c4. repro (short):
```\ncurl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":1024}' \\n  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate\n```
Responses show 502 with body: "upstream connection reset". Customer says failures spike when requests include large context (>=50k tokens) and billing header present.

ana (eng-runtime): interesting — we rolled tiny auth cache change at 08:55. not seeing infra deploys near 09:10 though. can you also attach an envoy upstream log?

jess (support): attaching snippet from customer curl and our edge logs: 
```\n[envoy] 2026-03-17T09:11:02Z upstream reset_inline error: connection reset by peer, upstream_host: 10.23.5.12:8080, response_code: 502\n[edge] request_id=trace-0a12b3c4 route=/v1/generate auth=200 billing-header=present payload_size=612345\n```

infra-bot: detected auth-service token-rotation job at 08:56:12 UTC on team-auth (job=auth-rotate-v2). 200/200 healthy, but increased latency to auth.lookup from 8ms->120ms for ~3m.

mike (sre): putting hypothesis: auth-cache rotation caused auth lookup latency -> upstream connection tieups -> envoy upstream resets for long-lived streaming/generator connections. large payloads keep connections busy, exhaust keepalive pool. can someone repro locally with auth stubs?

ana (eng-runtime): repro steps I ran:
1) start a small local envoy with upstream pool size=50 and keepalive=60s.
2) spike auth latency to 150ms.
3) send concurrent streaming requests with payload ~600KB and long KV cache loads.
Result: upstream 502s and connection resets after pool exhaustion.

mike (sre): mitigation plan:
- short term: increase envoy upstream_http2_connection_pool_size for hosted edge by +30% and raise max concurrent streams to avoid immediate resets. roll config to canary.
- mid term: add backoff in auth lookup and graceful queueing for long-lived generator requests.
- customer-facing: notify acme-inc we've identified auth-rotation spike + long payloads causing keepalive exhaustion; temporary suggestion to reduce concurrency or split requests.

jess (support): I've drafted customer message and opened escalation jira INF-4592. tagging @ana @mike for the canary. :thumbsup:

ana (eng-runtime): also adding a small server-side change: if billing header present and payload > 256KB, prefer non-streaming short-lived connection (fallback) until auth-cache stabilizes. will PR later today.

mike (sre): good. I'll kick the canary config change and monitor 1min error-rate and latency dashboards. if error-rate drops -> promote. setting alert: edge.502_rate > 1% for 5m triggers pager.

customer_alert_bot: message delivered to acme-inc support contact at 09:33 UTC (ticket #ACME-987).

jess (support): thanks everyone. I'll keep thread updated with canary metrics and customer replies.
